---
title: "Notation and algebra contracts"
---

The same symbol can denote very different operations in contest editorials.
These notes use the following conventions unless a chapter overrides them.

## Coefficients and residues

- $\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$ denotes the nonnegative integers; $[0,n)$ denotes integer
  indices $0,\ldots,n-1$ when used for arrays. Empty sums are zero and empty
  products are one. A combinatorial empty object is counted once.
- $[P]$ is the indicator of proposition $P$; this is different from coefficient
  extraction $[x^n]$. $\binom nk=0$ when $n\ge0$ and $k<0$ or $k>n$.
- $\forall$ means “for every,” $\exists$ means “there exists,” and $\iff$
  requires both implications. [Chapter 00](00-foundations/chapter.qmd)
  explains proof and set notation.

- $[x^{n}]F(x)$ is the coefficient of $x^{n}$.
- $\mathbb Z/m\mathbb Z$ is the ring of residues modulo $m$.
- $\mathbb F_p$ is a field only when $p$ is prime.
- $\mathbb F_q$ denotes a finite field of prime-power size $q=p^r$ when
  explicitly constructed; it is not the residue ring modulo $p^r$ for $r>1$.
  The *characteristic* is $p$: adding one to itself $p$ times gives zero.
  Characteristic zero means no positive number of copies of one gives zero.
- `mint` denotes a modular-integer type whose modulus is stated nearby.
- Division by $a$ means multiplication by $a^{-1}$ and therefore requires that
  $a$ be a unit.  In $\mathbb F_p$ this is equivalent to $a\ne0$; modulo a
  composite $m$ it is equivalent to $\gcd(a,m)=1$.
- For nonzero $n$, $v_p(n)$ is the exponent of prime $p$ in $n$; when needed,
  $v_p(0)=+\infty$.

## Arithmetic functions

- $\mathbf 1(n)=1$, $\varepsilon(1)=1$ and $\varepsilon(n)=0$ for $n>1$.
- $\mu$, $\varphi$, and $\tau$ are the Möbius, Euler-totient, and divisor-count
  functions.
- Dirichlet convolution is
  $(f*g)(n)=\sum_{d\mid n}f(d)g(n/d)$; its identity is $\varepsilon$.
- A function is multiplicative when $f(1)=1$ and
  $f(ab)=f(a)f(b)$ for $\gcd(a,b)=1$; "completely multiplicative" drops the
  coprimality requirement.

## Polynomial and series operations

- Polynomials and formal power series are coefficient arrays in increasing
  degree order.
- $F\bmod x^{n}$ means retain degrees $0,\ldots,n-1$.
- Multiplicative inverse $F^{-1}$ requires $F(0)$ to be a unit.
- Formal $\log F$ is normalized to constant term zero and normally requires
  $F(0)=1$; formal $\exp F$ normally requires $F(0)=0$.
- Computing these normalized series modulo $x^n$ by integration/factorial
  formulas requires $1,\ldots,n-1$ to be units. Over $\mathbb F_p$,
  $n\le p$ suffices. Set series on $n$ labels using ordinary factorial
  formulas instead need $1,\ldots,n$ units, hence $p>n$.
- Formal composition $F(G(x))$ is automatically well-defined for arbitrary
  infinite FPS only when $G(0)=0$.  Truncated or polynomial cases may allow
  more.
- Compositional inverse/reversion requires $F(0)=0$ and $F'(0)$ a unit.
- NTT length and root-of-unity conditions are part of an algorithm's contract,
  not implementation trivia.
- $\binom nr_q$ is a Gaussian/q-binomial coefficient; the subscript is a
  numerical field size or formal variable, not the arithmetic modulus.
- A set power series has coefficients $F[S]$ and multiplication
  $(FG)[S]=\sum_{T\subseteq S}F[T]G[S\setminus T]$.
- $F^{(j)}$ denotes the $j$th formal derivative; in a set-series chapter a
  partial derivative with respect to an element variable is named explicitly.

## Matrix and holonomic notation

- $\operatorname{Pf}(A)$ is the Pfaffian of an even skew-symmetric matrix;
  over characteristic other than two, $\operatorname{Pf}(A)^{2}=\det A$.
- $\operatorname{adj}(A)$ is the adjugate and satisfies
  $A\operatorname{adj}(A)=\det(A)I$ even when $A$ is singular.
- A P-recursive sequence satisfies a fixed-order recurrence with polynomial
  coefficients in the index.  A D-finite series satisfies a linear
  differential equation with polynomial coefficients.
- Classical D-finite closure statements are characteristic-zero results.
  Modular computation requires checking every denominator and singular index.

## Transforms

- Subsets are bitmasks when the ground set is $[0,n)$.
- The subset zeta transform sends $f(S)$ to $\sum_{T\subseteq S}f(T)$.
- XOR/AND/OR convolution names refer to the operation combining indices, not
  the pointwise operation after transformation.
- "Möbius inversion" may mean inversion on subsets, the divisor poset, or a
  general locally finite poset.  The chapter always names the order relation.

## Complexity

- $M(n)$ denotes the cost of multiplying degree-below-$n$ polynomials; with a
  suitable NTT, $M(n)=O(n\log n)$.
- A bound such as $O(M(n))$ can conceal a large constant and strict modulus
  requirements.  Use the actual maximum degree and transform count when judging
  feasibility.
- Randomized algorithms state whether their guarantee is Las Vegas (always
  correct, random time) or Monte Carlo (small error probability).

## Arithmetic conventions

- Signed overflow is never intentional.  Products near the 64-bit boundary use
  `__int128` or an explicitly justified unsigned technique.
- Routine algorithms are assumed to come from the reader's tested library; the
  notes state the contracts and arithmetic assumptions needed to select them.
- A product of two arbitrary unsigned 64-bit values fits in an unsigned
  128-bit integer, but may not fit in a signed 128-bit integer. An extra sum
  or product can overflow either. Bounds must cover every intermediate;
  use arbitrary-precision integers when fixed-width bounds fail.

## Formal Power Series & Generating Functions Track (`Ch 01`–`Ch 24`) {#fps-notation}

The 24-chapter FPS & Generating Functions track enforces the following canonical ring, operator, and defensive-contract notation across all chapters, checkpoints, and capstones:

### Rings, Valuations, and Formal Laurent Residues

- **Formal Power Series Ring $K[[x]]$**: For a commutative ring $K$ with unity, $K[[x]]$ is the ring of infinite formal series $F(x) = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} f_n x^n$ equipped with Cauchy convolution $[x^n](F \cdot G) = \sum_{i+j=n} f_i g_j$.
- **$x$-Adic Valuation $\nu(F) = \operatorname{val}(F) = \operatorname{ord}_x(F)$**: The valuation (or order, also written $\operatorname{val}_x(F)$ or $\operatorname{ord}_x(F)$) of $F(x) \in K((x))$ is the lowest index of a non-zero coefficient:
  $$\nu(F) = \operatorname{val}(F) = \operatorname{ord}_x(F) = \min\{n \in \mathbb{Z} : [x^n]F(x) \neq 0\}, \qquad \nu(0) = +\infty.$$
  An infinite sum $\sum_{k \ge 0} F_k(x)$ or infinite product $\prod_{k \ge 1}(1 + G_k(x))$ converges in the $x$-adic topology if and only if $\lim_{k \to \infty} \nu(F_k) = +\infty$ (respectively $\lim_{k \to \infty} \nu(G_k) = +\infty$).
- **Unit Criterion in $K[[x]]^\times$**: $F(x) \in K[[x]]$ has a multiplicative inverse $F(x)^{-1} \in K[[x]]$ if and only if its constant term is a unit in $K$: $[x^0]F(x) \in K^\times$.
- **Formal Laurent Series Ring $K((x))$**: $K((x)) = K[[x]][x^{-1}]$ consists of formal series $A(x) = \sum_{n=v}^{\infty} a_n x^n$ with finite lower bound $v \in \mathbb{Z}$ (at most finitely many negative powers of $x$). When $K$ is a field, $K((x))$ is the fraction field of $K[[x]]$.
- **Formal Residue Operator $\operatorname{Res}_{x=0} = \operatorname{Res}_x$**: For $F(x) \in K((x))$, the formal residue is purely algebraic:
  $$\operatorname{Res}_{x=0} F(x) = \operatorname{Res}_x F(x) = \operatorname{Res}_{x=0} F(x)\,dx = [x^{-1}]F(x).$$
  It satisfies $\operatorname{Res}_{x=0} A'(x) = 0$ for all $A(x) \in K((x))$ in every characteristic, and Jacobi's Formal Change-of-Variables Formula for any $G(u) \in K[[u]]$ with $\nu(G) = 1$ and $[u^1]G(u) \in K^\times$:
  $$\operatorname{Res}_{x=0} F(x)\,dx = \operatorname{Res}_{u=0} F(G(u))\,G'(u)\,du.$$
- **5-Ring Bivariate Hierarchy (`Ch 15`–`Ch 17`)**:
  1. $K[y][[x]]$ — polynomials in $y$ over $x$-power series ($\deg_y f_n(y) < \infty$ for each $n$);
  2. $(K[y, y^{-1}])[[x]]$ — Laurent polynomials in $y$ at each power of $x$ (the natural ring for 1D lattice walk step polynomials, where substituting a small root $y = y_0(x)$ with $\nu_x(y_0) \ge 1$ converges in the $x$-adic topology);
  3. $K[[x, y]]$ — formal power series in two commuting variables (supporting arbitrary $(n, m) \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}^2$);
  4. $K((x))[[y]]$ — formal power series in $y$ over the Laurent field $K((x))$ (bounded below in $x$ for each fixed $y^m$; note that $K((x))[[y]]$ and $K((y))[[x]]$ are **not** isomorphic: $\frac{1}{x - y} = \sum_{k \ge 0} x^{-k-1} y^k \in K((x))[[y]]$ vs. $-\sum_{k \ge 0} x^k y^{-k-1} \in K((y))[[x]]$);
  5. $K((z))[[t]]$ — formal power series in $t$ over the Laurent field $K((z))$ (the **Furstenberg Diagonal Ring**, where $x = z, \, y = t z^{-1}$ converts $[x^n y^n]F(x, y)$ into the 1D residue $[t^n]\operatorname{Res}_{z=0}\bigl(z^{-1}F(z, t z^{-1})\bigr)$ because each fixed power $t^k$ has Laurent $z$-valuation bounded below by $-k$).

### Hadamard Products, Diagonals, Differential & Transposed Operators

- **Hadamard Product $F \odot G$**: Termwise (coefficient-wise) product of two univariate series:
  $$(F \odot G)(x) = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \bigl([x^n]F(x)\bigr)\bigl([x^n]G(x)\bigr) x^n.$$
- **Constant-Term & Diagonal Operator $\operatorname{Diag}_{x,y}$**: For $F(x,y) = \sum_{i,j \ge 0} f_{i,j} x^i y^j$, the main diagonal is extracted via the Laurent substitution $x = u, y = t/u$ in $K[[t]]((u))$:
  $$\operatorname{Diag}_{x,y} F(x,y) = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} f_{n,n} t^n = [u^0] F(u, t/u) = \operatorname{Res}_{u=0} \frac{1}{u} F(u, t/u).$$
- **Euler Differential Operator $\vartheta$ (and Pointing $\Theta$, $\vartheta_x = x D_x$, $\Theta_x = x \partial_x$)**:
  $$\vartheta = \Theta = x \frac{d}{dx}, \qquad \vartheta^k\!\left(\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} f_n x^n\right) = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} n^k f_n x^n = \sum_{j=0}^{k} \left\{\begin{matrix} k \\ j \end{matrix}\right\} x^j F^{(j)}(x).$$
- **Weyl Algebra $K[x]\langle D \rangle$ & Shift Algebra $K[n]\langle E_n \rangle$**: Non-commutative operator rings governed by the Leibniz commutation relations:
  $$D x - x D = 1 \quad \text{in } K[x]\langle D \rangle, \qquad E_n n - (n + 1) E_n = 0 \quad \text{in } K[n]\langle E_n \rangle,$$
  connected on coefficients via $[x^n]\bigl(x^a D^b F(x)\bigr) = (n - a + 1)^{\overline{b}} f_{n - a + b}$.
- **Tellegen Transposed Multiplication (Middle Product `mulT` / $\operatorname{mulT}(C, B)$ / $\operatorname{mul}^T$)**: Given $B(x)$ of degree $< m$ and $C(x)$ of degree $< m + n - 1$, the transposed multiplication $\operatorname{mulT}(C, B) = T_B^\top \mathbf{c}$ (also written $\operatorname{mul}^T(B, C)$) is the linear transpose of $A \mapsto A \cdot B$ on the dual space $K[x]_{<n+m-1}^* \to K[x]_{<n}^*$:
  $$[x^i]\operatorname{mulT}(C, B) = \sum_{j=0}^{m-1} b_j c_{i+j} = [x^i]\bigl(B(x^{-1}) C(x)\bigr) \qquad (0 \le i < n).$$
- **$q$-Pochhammer Symbol & Gaussian $q$-Binomial Coefficient**:
  $$(a; q)_n = \prod_{i=0}^{n-1} (1 - a q^i), \qquad (a; q)_0 = 1, \qquad \begin{bmatrix} n \\ k \end{bmatrix}_q = \binom{n}{k}_q = \frac{(q; q)_n}{(q; q)_k (q; q)_{n-k}}.$$
- **Set Power Series Ring $\mathcal{R}_n$ & Dirichlet Ring $\mathcal{D}_f$**:
  $$\mathcal{R}_n = K[x_1, \dots, x_n]/(x_1^2, \dots, x_n^2), \qquad \mathcal{D}_f(s) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{f(n)}{n^s}, \qquad (\vartheta_{\Omega} f)(n) = \Omega(n) f(n).$$

### Master Operator & Symbol Table (`Ch 01`–`Ch 24`)

| Symbol / Operator | Mathematical Definition & Canonical Meaning | Local Algebraic Hypothesis |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| $[x^n] F(x)$, $[x^k y^m] F(x,y)$ | Coefficient extraction: $[x^n] \sum f_k x^k := f_n$; multivariate $[x^k y^m] F(x,y) := [x^k]\big([y^m] F(x,y)\big) = f_{k,m}$ | None (pure $K$-linear functional) |
| $F(x) \bmod x^N$ | Degree truncation: projection onto $R[x]/(x^N)$, keeping terms $x^0, \dots, x^{N-1}$ | None |
| $\deg(P)$ | Degree of a polynomial $P \in R[x]$, with $\deg(0) := -\infty$ | $P$ is a finite polynomial |
| $\nu(F) = \operatorname{val}(F) = \operatorname{ord}_x(F)$ | Formal ($\mathfrak{m}$-adic) valuation: $\min\{n \in \mathbb{Z} : [x^n]F(x) \neq 0\}$, with $\nu(0) := +\infty$ (written $\operatorname{val}_x(F)$ or $\operatorname{ord}_x(F)$ when the variable is emphasized) | None |
| $D F(x) = F'(x)$ | Formal derivative: $\sum_{n \ge 1} n f_n x^{n-1}$ | None |
| $\int F(x)\,dx$ | Formal integral: $\sum_{n \ge 0} \frac{f_n}{n+1} x^{n+1}$ (constant term $0$) | $1, 2, \dots, N \in R^\times$ ($\operatorname{char}(K) = 0$ or $p > N$) |
| $\vartheta = x D$ (or $\vartheta_x = x D_x$, $\Theta_x = x \partial_x$) | Theta / Euler pointing operator: $\vartheta F(x) = x F'(x) = \sum_{n \ge 0} n f_n x^n$ | None |
| $E$ (or $E_n$) and $\Delta = E - I$ | Forward shift operator ($E f_n = f_{n+1}$) and forward difference operator ($\Delta f_n = f_{n+1} - f_n$) | None |
| $\operatorname{Res}_{x=0} F(x) = \operatorname{Res}_x F(x)$ | Formal residue (also written $\operatorname{Res}_{x=0} F(x)\,dx$): $[x^{-1}] F(x)$ for $F(x) \in K((x))$ | $F(x) \in K((x))$ is a formal Laurent series |
| $\operatorname{Diag}_{x,y} F(x,y)$ | Bivariate diagonal operator: $\sum_{n \ge 0} ([x^n y^n] F(x,y)) t^n$ | $F(x,y) \in K[[x,y]]$ (or diagonally summable Laurent series) |
| $\operatorname{mulT}(C, B) = T_B^\top \mathbf{c}$ | Transposed multiplication (middle product) on the dual space $K[x]_{<n+m-1}^* \to K[x]_{<n}^*$: $[x^i]\operatorname{mulT}(C, B) := \sum_{j=0}^{m-1} b_j c_{i+j}$ | None |
| $x^{\underline{k}}$, $x^{\overline{k}}$ | Falling factorial $x(x-1)\cdots(x-k+1)$ and rising factorial $x(x+1)\cdots(x+k-1)$ | None |
| $\left\{ \begin{matrix} n \\ k \end{matrix} \right\}$, $\left[ \begin{matrix} n \\ k \end{matrix} \right]$, $\left\langle \begin{matrix} n \\ k \end{matrix} \right\rangle$ | Stirling numbers of the second kind, unsigned Stirling numbers of the first kind, and Eulerian numbers (Karamata notation) | None |
| $\begin{bmatrix} n \\ k \end{bmatrix}_q$, $(a; q)_n$ | Gaussian $q$-binomial coefficient $\frac{(q;q)_n}{(q;q)_k (q;q)_{n-k}}$ and $q$-Pochhammer symbol $\prod_{j=0}^{n-1}(1 - a q^j)$ | None (polynomial in $q$) |
| $*_{\text{or}}$, $*_{\text{and}}$, $*_{\text{xor}}$, $*_{\text{sub}}$ | Bitwise OR, AND, XOR convolutions on $K^{2^n}$ and subset convolution on $K[x_0,\dots,x_{n-1}]/(x_0^2,\dots,x_{n-1}^2)$ | $*_{\text{xor}}$ inversion requires $2 \in K^\times$ ($\operatorname{char}(K) \neq 2$) |

### The 10 Global Algebraic Failure Modes (Plus Extensions `#11`–`#16`) {#fps-failure-modes}

Every algorithm contract in the 24-chapter FPS textbook cross-references these canonical failure modes:

| Failure Mode | Hazard Name & Algebraic Trigger | Exact Defensive Remedy & Target Chapter |
| :-: | :--- | :--- |
| **Failure Mode #1** | **Precision Loss in Shifted Division $B(x)/A(x) \bmod x^N$** when $\nu(A) = v \ge 1$ | Dividing by $x^v$ shifts degree $N+v-1$ down to $N-1$; always compute both $A(x)$ and $B(x)$ to precision **$\bmod x^{N+v}$** before shifting (`Ch 01.4`). |
| **Failure Mode #2** | **3-Way Modular Reduction Trap in $P(x)^\alpha \bmod x^N$** when $\alpha \ge p$ | (1) Shift $v \cdot \alpha$ in true integer `__int128` (return $0$ if $v > 0$ and $v\alpha \ge N$); (2) leading scalar $c_v^{\alpha \bmod (p-1)}$ by Fermat; (3) series exponent $(\alpha \bmod p)\ln \widetilde{P}$ (`Ch 02.3`). |
| **Failure Mode #3** | **Rational Exponent $P(x)^{a/b}$ Existence Failure** ($\gcd(a,b)=1$) | $P(x)^{a/b} \in \mathbb{F}_p[[x]]$ exists iff **$b \mid (v \cdot a)$ in $\mathbb{Z}$** and the leading coefficient $c_v$ is a **$b$-th residue in $\mathbb{F}_p^\times$** (`Ch 02.3`). |
| **Failure Mode #4** | **Characteristic-$p$ Transcendental Breakdown ($\ln, \exp, \int$)** when $p \le N$ | $\int x^{p-1}dx = x^p/p$ divides by $0 \bmod p$; replace $\ln/\exp$ with algebraic `inv`, Bostan–Mori, Frobenius $A(x)^p \equiv A(x^p) \pmod p$, or Boxed Products (`Ch 02.2`, `Ch 04.3`). |
| **Failure Mode #5** | **Lagrange Inversion $1/n$ Breakdown** when $p \mid n$ | Classical LIF $\frac{1}{n}[u^{n-1}]H'(u)\Phi(u)^n$ divides by $n \equiv 0 \pmod p$; always use **Derivative-Free Residue LIF (Form 2)**: $[u^n]H(u)(\Phi(u) - u\Phi'(u))\Phi(u)^{n-1}$ (`Ch 11.2`). |
| **Failure Mode #6** | **Compositional Inverse (`revert`) Breakdown** when $p \le N$ | Route A (`noshi91` Power Projection + `pow`) divides by $1, \dots, N-1$; switch to **Route B (Newton Iteration + Kinoshita–Li `compose`)**, which divides only by $2$ and $f_1$ (`Ch 21.4`). |
| **Failure Mode #7** | **2D Obstinate Kernel Over-Subtraction & Newton–Girard Symmetric Function Asymmetry ($p_k \leftrightarrow e_k$)** when $p \le N$ | Subtracting $F(x,0)+F(0,y)$ double-counts $F(0,0)$ ($\to +F(0,0)$); for $E(t) = \sum_{k \ge 0} e_k t^k$, $e_k \to p_k$ via $P(t) = -t E'(-t)/E(-t)$ uses only `inv` ($e_0=1$) and is **100% division-free in all characteristics $p$**; $p_k \to e_k$ divides by $k$ and fails for $p \le N$ (`Ch 17.3`). |
| **Failure Mode #8** | **Vanishing Indicial Polynomial $I(n^*) \equiv 0 \pmod p$** in P-Recursive Unrolling | Supply initial value if $I(n^*) = 0$ in $\mathbb{Z}$; lift the recurrence to the **$p$-adic quotient ring $\mathbb{Z}/p^{V+1}\mathbb{Z}$** ($u \cdot p^e$) where $V = \sum_{I(n)\equiv 0} v_p(I(n))$ (`Ch 18.4`). |
| **Failure Mode #9** | **Gaussian $q$-Binomial Pole** when $\operatorname{ord}_p(q) = d \le n$ | Direct $(q;q)_n$ division hits $1 - q^d \equiv 0 \pmod p$; apply the **$q$-Lucas Theorem** $\begin{bmatrix} n_1 d + n_0 \\ k_1 d + k_0 \end{bmatrix}_q \equiv \binom{n_1}{k_1}\begin{bmatrix} n_0 \\ k_0 \end{bmatrix}_q \pmod p$ (`Ch 23.2`). |
| **Failure Mode #10** | **Dynamic Division by Zero in Point-Value / Tree-DP Products** | When a light child evaluates to $F_v(\omega_r) \equiv 0 \pmod p$, maintain each frequency state in the **Zero-Divisor Monoid $(a, c) \equiv a \cdot 0^c$** ($a \in \mathbb{F}_p^\times, c \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$) (`Ch 22.3`). |
| **Failure Mode #11** | **Missing $m$-th Root of Unity in Filter (`单位根反演`)** when $m \nmid (p-1)$ | Do not search for a scalar $\omega_m \in \mathbb{F}_p$; compute modulo the **Cyclotomic Polynomial $\Phi_m(\omega)$** in $\mathbb{F}_p[\omega]/(\Phi_m(\omega))$ (`Ch 07.4`). |
| **Failure Mode #12** | **Bluestein Chirp-Z Square-Root Failure ($c^{1/2} \notin \mathbb{F}_p$) & $c=0$ Trap** | Never use $ij = \frac{1}{2}((i+j)^2 - i^2 - j^2)$; always use **Bluestein's Binomial Identity $ij = \binom{i+j}{2} - \binom{i}{2} - \binom{j}{2}$**, and branch on $c = 0$ (`Ch 07.3`). |
| **Failure Mode #13** | **Full-Online Self-Convolution Asymmetry Bug at $l > 0$** | In `cdq(l, r)` for $f_n = \sum_{i=1}^{n-1} f_i f_{n-i}$, convolve $f[0..m]^2$ at $l=0$, but convolve **$2 \cdot f[l..m] \times f[0..r-l]$ at $l > 0$** (`Ch 09.2`). |
| **Failure Mode #14** | **Negative-Integer $\alpha = -d$ Pole in Generalized $\alpha$-Euler Transform** | Split $F(y) = F_{\le d}(y) + y^{d+1} F_{>d}(y)$ before applying $(1-x)^{-\alpha}$ so the tail shifts $\alpha \mapsto 1 > 0$ (`Ch 06.4`). |
| **Failure Mode #15** | **Hidden Pole at $z = 0$ in Improper Rational Diagonals** ($\deg_y A \ge \deg_y B$) | Substituting $y = t/z$ introduces $z^{\deg_y B - \deg_y A - 1}$; include $\operatorname{Res}_{z=0}$ or perform polynomial division in $y$ first (`Ch 16.4`). |
| **Failure Mode #16** | **Catalan Negative Upper-Index Trap ($k=0$) & Prüfer $N=1$ Trap** | Isolate $k=0$ before $\binom{2k-1}{k} = \binom{2k-1}{k-1}$ ($\binom{-1}{0}=1 \neq \binom{-1}{-1}=0$), and handle $N=1$ before $(N-2)!$ Prüfer extraction (`Ch 04.4`, `Ch 11.3`). |
